rules: Every record remains a candidate until human review.
Similarity does not imply historical descent, common origin, or diffusion.
Field discoveries remain separate from peer-reviewed evidence until formal publication or authoritative specialist documentation supports promotion.
Human remains, mortuary contexts, and living/traditional religious knowledge require cultural-sensitivity review before public presentation.
Publication/index dates are preserved separately; indexing novelty is not publication novelty.

new_candidates.title: Stratigraphic and chronological evidence for overlapping Bronze Age tomb types in the Khaybar region, Saudi Arabia
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: New stratigraphy and radiocarbon dates refine the sequence of Khaybar funerary monument types, including expansion around 2200 BCE, decline after 2000 BCE, and appearance of small alveolus tower-tombs around 1900–1800 BCE.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: A refined regional funerary chronology does not by itself identify ancestry, migration, cult continuity, or causal cultural transmission. Human remains are poorly preserved and interpretations remain context-specific.

new_candidates.title: Of snakes and gods: early evidence for the cult of Sabazios in the Roman villa of Collet
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Formal comparison, laboratory analysis and 3D modelling support an author interpretation linking a snake-headed vessel from an Augustan-period rural villa to Sabazios, extending the review surface for cult distribution beyond urban settings.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Snake iconography is not unique to Sabazios and the paper itself frames the identification and diffusion implications as an argument. Do not create a historical-diffusion edge or provenance claim without direct review of comparative objects and context.

new_candidates.title: Magical thinking, folklore, and pluralities of belief: Death omens in nineteenth-century rural England
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: The article argues that death-omen practices could coexist with religion, science and partial skepticism, and explicitly warns that customary engagement with omens does not establish firm propositional belief.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Folklore collections are mediated historical sources with collection bias. Practice, narration, custom and belief should remain distinct coded variables.

new_candidates.title: Immersive virtual reality: distinct impact on altered states of consciousness
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: With the same emotionally evocative content, immersive VR produced higher MEQ30 scores than standard-screen viewing, supplying experimental support for separating induction medium/context from phenomenological outcome.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: MEQ30 scores are psychometric reports and do not establish metaphysical content, historical ritual equivalence, or identity with psychedelic states.

new_candidates.title: Epipaleolithic turtle figurines from Gedikkaya Hill and İn Cave, Bilecik, Türkiye
new_candidates.provenance: Anadolu Agency report on excavations led by Prof. Deniz Sarı, Bilecik Şeyh Edebali University, on behalf of Türkiye’s Culture and Tourism Ministry.

dating.method: radiocarbon dates on archaeological context as reported

new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Approximately 25 limestone turtle-shaped objects, some clay-coated and several inserted around circular stone arrangements, provide a potentially important deep-time material-context candidate.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: The reported dates apply to associated archaeological contexts, not necessarily direct dating of each figurine. Ritual purpose and turtle symbolism are excavator interpretations and must remain separate from the observed placement and morphology.

contradictions_or_pressure.finding: The death-omens study explicitly argues that participation in customary omen practices need not imply firm propositional belief.
contradictions_or_pressure.action: Review whether NOEMA separately codes practice, reported credence, social function and propositional belief.

contradictions_or_pressure.finding: The Sabazios vessel is a strong contextual identification candidate but snake imagery is not unique to one cult; iconographic similarity alone cannot establish descent or diffusion.
contradictions_or_pressure.action: Require contextual, chronological and comparative evidence before adding a cult-spread relationship.

contradictions_or_pressure.finding: Immersive presentation changed mystical-type scores despite constant content, pressuring any model that treats phenomenology as determined by substance or content alone.
contradictions_or_pressure.action: Keep induction medium, setting/context, expectation and phenomenology as separable dimensions.

contradictions_or_pressure.finding: The priority item titled 'Some New World: Myths of Supernatural Belief in a Secular Age' is dated 2026-09-01 in the discovery artifact, while external bibliographic sources identify the same title as a Cambridge University Press monograph first published in 2024; the Crossref DOI may represent a distinct review or derivative record and requires identity verification.
contradictions_or_pressure.action: Do not ingest as a new primary research publication until DOI-level source identity is inspected.

dating_revisions.scope: Regional Bronze Age funerary chronology, Khaybar oasis
dating_revisions.finding: New radiocarbon and stratigraphic evidence refines overlap and transition among tomb types, including large tailed tombs/other tower-tombs and later small alveolus tower-tombs.
dating_revisions.impact: Candidate chronology refinement; review against any existing Khaybar or Northwest Arabia temporal assertions before modifying them.
